alert.caveat: It may be none of these. Measured across this project, 41 of 41 long stretches of activity resolved on their own — so treat this as a question, not a verdict.
alert.churn.title: Rewritten {n}× in {m} min
alert.churn.body: This file was written {n} times inside {m} minutes. That is usually one of three things: genuine iteration, a fix that keeps regressing, or two concerns living in one file and being edited alternately.
alert.churn.prompt: {path} was rewritten {n} times in {m} minutes. Before changing anything, read the file’s recent history and determine why: (a) genuine iteration toward a goal, (b) a fix that keeps regressing, or (c) two concerns in one file being edited alternately. Report which, with evidence. If (b), find the root cause rather than reapplying the fix — state what makes it revert. If (c), name the concerns and propose a split. If (a), say so and stop; repeated edits are not by themselves a problem. Do not refactor before answering.
alert.collision.title: {n} lines, edited by 2 sessions {s}s apart
alert.collision.body: Two concurrent sessions wrote this file within {s} seconds of each other, and it is {n} lines long. On a file this size that usually means it has become a junction — somewhere many unrelated tasks have to touch.
alert.collision.prompt: {path} is {n} lines and was edited by two concurrent sessions within {s} seconds of each other. Analyse whether it has become a junction — a file many unrelated tasks must touch. List its distinct responsibilities with the line ranges for each. If there are three or more with little shared state, propose a split: name the new modules, what moves, and what imports change. If the responsibilities are genuinely one thing, say so and explain what made the collision look structural. Propose only; do not move code yet.
alert.stalled.title: {n} calls over {m} min, nothing written
alert.stalled.body: {n} tool calls have run over the last {m} minutes without a single file being written. Calls landing with nothing produced is the one signal here that means look now — reading, searching and thinking are normal, but not this long with no result.
alert.stalled.prompt: You have run {n} tool calls over {m} minutes without writing to any file. Stop and report, in this order: what you are currently trying to establish, what you have ruled out, and what is blocking the next edit. If you are waiting on something that will not arrive, say so. If you have been re-reading the same files, name them and state what you expected to find. Do not resume work until you have answered.
